newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra launches mining environment code.
newsitem.headline: Canberra launches mining environment code.

text.p: The Australian government launched on Tuesday a code aimed at boosting mining companies' concern for the impact of their industry on the environment.

Minerals Council of Australia president Jerry Ellis, chairman elect The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said the code provided a rigorous framework to guide mining companies towards effective environmental management strategies for each phase of mine development. "More than in any other way, the community judges the minerals industry by its environmental performance," Ellis said in a statement.
Ellis said very few companies would be able to comply immediately with the voluntary code's standards, although 18 companies had already committed to it.
The code required companies to prepare public annual reports on code implementation and on their environmental performance.
Externally accredited auditors would evaluate implementation of the code at least every three years, Ellis said.
"The code's bottom line objective is improved environmental performance across the industry," he said.
"Ultimately that will be the test of the code's success."
